What Airbnb Holders Bought Into

If you only skimmed the 2025 debate on Airbnb, with bulls calling it a lifestyle platform in the making and bears warning of regulatory walls and slowing core markets, you might not have expected the outcome. Holding Airbnb over the past year would have returned 49.5%, including dividends. If you had faced that split view back in November 2025, what in the record could have justified taking the risk anyway?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The easy part of this move is behind Airbnb. Zero in on 32 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.

The Two Airbnb Stories Investors Were Choosing Between

The shares cost US$123 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Airbnb then had to pick between two very different but reasonable stories about what that price implied.

On the bullish side, the July 2025 Narrative from User argued Airbnb could justify a Fair Value of US$164, built on revenue growth of 12.0% and a 25.0% profit margin as it pushed further into lifestyle use cases and international markets.

The May 2025 bearish case pointed to a Fair Value of US$96, stressing regulatory pressure, housing affordability criticism, and the risk that tighter rules and compliance costs would restrict listings and squeeze profitability.

NasdaqGS:ABNB 1-Year Stock Price Chart
What The Airbnb Evidence Actually Tested

Airbnb's Q3 2026 report showed revenue at US$4.9b and net income at US$1.9b, with net margin moving from 33.6% in Q3 2025 to 38.8%. That combination supported the bullish Narrative that assumed strong profitability on a larger platform. Regulatory friction still appeared through actions such as Chicago's lawsuit, so the period's evidence pointed in both directions.

The key lesson is simple. When a story depends on "profitable at scale," focus on whether revenue, absolute earnings, and net margin all move together in the reported numbers, particularly once regulators begin to push back.

What Airbnb's Recent Run Already Prices In

Airbnb shares now trade at US$181 after gaining 49.5% over the past year, and the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sees its Fair Value as sitting below that level.

The Narrative leans on strong execution but argues much of the optimistic booking, margin, and AI story is already priced in. For today's valuation to hold, a buyer would need to assume Airbnb's AI rebuild and new services keep offsetting regulatory and platform disintermediation pressure without eroding profitability.

title: How Has Booking Holdings' Story Changed?

How Has Booking Holdings' Story Changed?

Booking Holdings (BKNG) stock trades at 16.7 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. Shareholders paying that price need to know what they are buying. On its fiscal Q4 2024 call in February 2025, management highlighted 19% growth in room nights booked at alternative accommodations. On its latest call, the first priority it discussed was AI. So what does management talk up now, and how big is it?

Booking Holdings Now Talks Up AI And Connected Trips

During its fiscal Q3 2026 call on November 3, 2026, management talked up new AI-native experiences built outside its existing brands. This includes Vayo, which management called "a proactive AI travel agent." The company also called its Connected Trip efforts and Genius loyalty program central to its goals. A Connected Trip is one where a traveler books more than one kind of travel with Booking.com.

Neither theme is new. In February 2025 management was already focusing more on its Connected Trip vision and pointing to AI offerings. Alternative accommodations still get a pitch, but a different one: on that call management called their growth strong, and on the latest call it pointed to growth picking up from the second quarter.

How Big Is Each Theme At Booking.com?

These initiatives fit within a broader business that generated $28.1 billion of revenue over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, up 8.0% from a year earlier. Alternative accommodations remain a large part of Booking.com, making up about 37% of its room nights in fiscal Q3 2026. Room nights for the category grew 7%, up from 4% in the second quarter. That pace matched the room night growth management gave for the whole company.

The Connected Trip is measured in transactions rather than room nights. Management said those transactions grew almost 20% from a year earlier and made up a low double-digit share of Booking.com's transactions.

The AI products are earlier still. Separately, visitors sent by AI language models, a third-party channel rather than a Booking product, still bring in well under 1% of Booking.com's room nights, management said. On October 14, 2026, the company announced a planned $100 million investment in Vayo, its new company.

Is Booking Holdings' Shift Good News For You?

On the figures so far, the shift looks more reassuring than concerning. Alternative accommodations are growing as fast as the company's room nights overall, and their listings growth accelerated to 9%, which management called an encouraging signal for future growth in that category. That category's room night growth of 7% is still well below the 19% management highlighted in February 2025.

During this period, the Zacks Leisure and Recreation Services industry, which Airbnb falls in, has gained 11.1%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Airbnb is expected to post earnings of $0.88 per share, indicating a change of +57.1% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +5% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.49 points to a change of +36.2% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +3.9%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $6.41 indicates a change of +16.7% from what Airbnb is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +4.7%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Airbnb is rated Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

title: Airbnb vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Airbnb vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool

Choosing between a global travel leader and a Latin American commerce giant requires balancing high growth against established profitability. Which path is right for your portfolio between Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI)?

Airbnb provides a unique global platform for alternative accommodations, while MercadoLibre operates an expansive ecosystem of e-commerce, fintech, and logistics services across Latin America. Both companies benefit from the digital shift in consumer spending, but they navigate very different competitive landscapes and regional economic conditions as they head toward 2027.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb connects over 5 million hosts with guests seeking unique stays and experiences in over 220 countries, as detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. Its two-sided platform offers hosts tools like integrated payments and protection through AirCover, while providing guests with AI-powered search and personalization features. By maintaining a marketplace rather than owning properties, the company stays lean while expanding its presence among travel and tourism stocks.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $12.3 billion, representing growth of approximately 10.8% compared to the previous year. The company reported net income of about $2.5 billion for the period. While revenue continued to climb, the net margin of roughly 20.4% was lower than in previous years as the company invested in platform updates and marketing.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating a conservative amount of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to cover short-term liabilities, is roughly 1.4x. In FY 2025, free cash flow reached around $4.6 billion, though stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a massive ecosystem in Latin America, which the company detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. It integrates a marketplace for buyers and sellers with its Mercado Pago fintech solution and a proprietary logistics network, Mercado Envios, to ensure fast delivery. This integrated approach creates a powerful flywheel where commerce, payments, and logistics reinforce one another for its 136 million unique buyers.

In FY 2025, revenue reached around $28.9 billion, a significant increase of approximately 39.1% compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of roughly $2.0 billion for the same period. While the top line grew rapidly, the net margin was approximately 6.9% as the company focused on market share expansion and its credit business.

Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB).

Airbnb currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.93, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 42 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.93 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 42 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 21 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 50% and 9.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for ABNB
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for ABNB

Check price target & stock forecast for Airbnb here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Airbnb, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Investors seek growth stocks to capitalize on above-average growth in financials that help these securities grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. However, it isn't easy to find a great growth stock.

In addition to volatility, these stocks carry above-average risk by their very nature. Also, one could end up losing from a stock whose growth story is actually over or nearing its end.

However, the task of finding cutting-edge growth stocks is made easy with the help of the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects.

Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) is on the list of such stocks currently recommended by our proprietary system. In addition to a favorable Growth Score, it carries a top Zacks Rank.

Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And returns are even better for stocks that possess the combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy).

While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this company is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:

Earnings Growth

Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. And for growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is definitely preferable, and often an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.

While the historical EPS growth rate for Airbnb is 22.4%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 36.2% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 27.3%.

Impressive Asset Utilization Ratio

Asset utilization ratio -- also known as sales-to-total-assets (S/TA) ratio -- is often overlooked by investors, but it is an important indicator in growth investing. This metric exhibits how efficiently a firm is utilizing its assets to generate sales.

Right now, Airbnb has an S/TA ratio of 0.55, which means that the company gets $0.55 in sales for each dollar in assets. Comparing this to the industry average of 0.52, it can be said that the company is more efficient.

While the level of efficiency in generating sales matters a lot, so does the sales growth of a company. And Airbnb is well positioned from a sales growth perspective too. The company's sales are expected to grow 17.3% this year versus the industry average of 3.7%.

We just published a list of the 10 Stocks Analysts Just Upgraded and Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) ranked 9th on this list.

Wall Street spent last Thursday reminding investors how quickly a favorite theme can turn. Worries that Democratic midterm wins could bring tighter rules for artificial intelligence and data centers sent technology stocks sharply lower. The damage spread well beyond the group that was under the microscope.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, its biggest one-day drop in 19 months, and closed more than 10% below its October record, a slide that put it in a correction. The S&P 500 lost 4.36%, its worst drop since the April 2025 tariff shock, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 3.44%. The drop more than erased the previous day's gain, the market's best in three months.

Trading was frantic. About 26.9 billion shares changed hands, against a 20-session average of 17.7 billion.

10 Unrivaled Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade

Photo by Arturo Añez on Unsplash

Chip Stocks Take the Heaviest Hit as AI Build-Out Fears Spread

Semiconductor stocks absorbed the worst of it, and the selling was heavy in the other stocks tied to data center spending too. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index dropped more than 12%, and S&P 500 companies lost about $3 trillion in market value in one session. Even so, the S&P 500 was still up 7.4% for the year, and the Nasdaq Composite was still up 4.6%.

"This feels like the capitulation phase for the data center capex beneficiary stocks, especially the semiconductors," Argent Capital Management portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek told Reuters. Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp, said investors were starting to price in the chance that newly elected lawmakers would slow the build-out. Our ranking of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50% or more upside covers more of the group.

Rate Worries and Oil Add Another Layer of Pressure

The selling landed on top of a tightening cycle. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin both hinted at possible future rate hikes. Traders expected the Federal Reserve to raise rates again next month after a September increase.

Energy prices added to the strain. Brent crude rose 3.9% to $98.29 a barrel, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.83% from 4.90%. Readers who follow analyst calls on value can find more ideas in our list of affordable stocks that Wall Street analysts like.

Overseas, the Bank of England raised its main rate for the first time in three years. Governor Andrew Bailey said, "The best thing that can happen is to resolve the conflict in the Middle East; there's no question about it."
